<div><div><div><div><div>Posted by [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/user2 rlpowell] on Fri 11 of Feb., 2005 19:14 GMT posts: 14214</div><div>
I suggest that these words be broken up into two basic types:

1. Words that fundamentally divide the number into two sections of 
distinct type: ce'i, fi'u, ki'o (sort of), pi, pi'e, ra'e

2. Words that scope to the right: ma'u, me'i, ni'u, za'u

Hmm. I thought ji'i was in this section, which is why I was writing 
this; it seems that ji'i should scope to the right.

Oh well; I think this breakdown still applies.

-Robin

<div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?forumId=1&comments_parentId=3872&comments_per_page=1&thread_style=commentStyle_plain BPFK Section: Syntactic Numbers]</div><br></div><div><div>Posted by [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/user6 xorxes] on Fri 11 of Feb., 2005 20:38 GMT posts: 1912</div><div>
> Hmm. I thought ji'i was in this section, which is why I was writing 
> this; it seems that ji'i should scope to the right.

ji'i, me'i and za'u are included in "Inexact numbers", because they 
are part of quantifiers. They go together with su'o and su'e. 
(da'a is not exactly in their group, but it also has scope to the right.)

mu'o mi'e xorxes
